newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour MP dies, Major back on level terms.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour MP dies, Major back on level terms.

text.p: Martin Redmond, a member of parliament for the main opposition Labour party, died on Monday after a long illness, the party said.
Redmond's death means that the ruling Conservative party now has exactly the same number of MPs, 322, as all other parties combined.

Prime Minister John Major had slipped into a minority of one in the lower House of Commons last week after the death of Conservative MP Iain Mills, heightening speculation that he might be forced into an early election.
Redmond, the MP for the Yorkshire mining constituency of Don Valley, had been ill with cancer for some time. He was 50 and had a solid majority of 13,534 at the 1992 election.
Major must hold Britain's election by May 22 at the latest. It was not immediately clear whether Labour would call a by-election for Redmond's seat before then.
